reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because the creator discusses personal experience with StrongBlock nodes and demonstrates how to reduce Ethereum transaction fees when withdrawing tokens or paying maintenance fees. He describes uncertain returns and market movements as personal speculation, not as a guaranteed profit, and the viewer action is a wallet fee-setting procedure rather than a solicitation to invest or send money to the creator.

opening.argument: Judge the fee tutorial alongside the return story. The speaker says his node purchases may repay their cost in less than 100 days, while the displayed dashboard pairs node rewards with controls to create a node and pay node fees. That connects the prospect of recovering an outlay to continued paid node participation. The instructions for lowering transaction fees can make that participation seem more manageable; they are not isolated from the financial proposition.

You can do the same thing for paying your monthly maintenance fees.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited wallet settings explain how to change a fee, but they do not address why the tutorial is attached to a node-return account. Calling the returns personal does not erase the example he gives of recovering his initial outlay in less than 100 days, or the node-creation control shown beside rewards.

citations.quote: so in m ly lucky case it'll take less than the usual 100 days to get back the USD amount that I put in to start these things up.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: That reading turns an account of existing purchases into an invitation to make new ones. The speaker qualifies the payback estimate as his lucky case, says he does not know when the price will recover, and explicitly teaches a maximum-fee setting for transactions. The dashboard shows his node interface, not an instruction to viewers to purchase nodes.

opening.argument: The combination deserves scrutiny: the speaker reports seven purchased nodes, two profitable withdrawals, and a possible payback period shorter than the stated usual 100 days. The dashboard shows rewards alongside node-creation and fee-payment controls. He also says withdrawing from seven nodes incurs gas seven times. Those details put an attractive return example beside repeated costs, while the headline promises lower fees. A careful judge could read the cost-saving pitch as making the node-return proposition more appealing, even though the account does not prove what a new participant would earn.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense cites uncertainty, but uncertainty does not make the favorable payback example disappear. Nor does a functioning fee-setting demonstration establish that the surrounding return story is merely neutral: the speaker places actual withdrawals and repeated node costs in the same account.

citations.quote: I've only taken profits 2 times, both times when strong was in the 600s
I'm taking strong out of seven different nodes so I'm paying gas on that 7 different times.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are risk signals, not evidence of a deceptive offer. The speaker calls his outcome lucky, says the market took a hard hit, and explains that setting the fee too low may leave a transaction pending indefinitely. Those caveats undercut an easy-return reading; the concrete instruction remains how to set a wallet fee.

opening.argument: The instructional format also gives the node activity a favorable frame. The speaker establishes himself as a repeat buyer, describes taking profits, then walks through making withdrawals and maintenance cheaper. The dashboard places rewards and a create-node control in the same view. Taken together, the lesson does more than explain a generic wallet setting: it presents paid nodes as an ongoing route to rewards whose operating costs can be reduced. That promotional effect matters when evaluating the video as a whole.

citations.quote: I've since bought a few more.
I've only taken profits 2 times, both times when strong was in the 600s
You can do the same thing for paying your monthly maintenance fees.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the Trust Wallet and MetaMask instructions are concrete, but that does not settle the video's role. The speaker frames those steps around extracting STRONG from nodes and paying their monthly maintenance, while showing a dashboard with rewards and node creation. Technical accuracy alone does not rule out promotion.

citations.quote: You can do the same thing for paying your monthly maintenance fees.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A demonstration involving someone's existing nodes is not, by itself, a solicitation to buy nodes. The stated purpose is to pay less in transaction fees, and the speaker explains the operational tradeoff: a lower maximum fee means waiting for network conditions, possibly without the transaction going through. His profit history supplies context, not a promise to viewers.
